question: Varun bought some erasers at the rate of ₹150/dozen. He sold them for ₹18 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 eraser = ₹150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5

SP of 1 eraser = ₹18

Ratio of CP to SP = 12.5 : 18 = 25 : 36

Profit in ratio = 36 − 25 = 11 parts

Profit % = (11 ÷ 25) × 100 = 44%

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 dozen (12) erasers = ₹150

Selling price of 1 eraser = ₹18

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP = ₹12.5
 (150 ÷ 12)
 
 SP = ₹18
 

 
 + ₹5.5
 Profit
 Profit % = (5.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 44%

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 eraser = 150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5

⇒ Profit = 18 − 12.5 = ₹5.5

⇒ Profit % = (5.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (55 ÷ 125) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (11 ÷ 25) × 100 = 11 × 4 = 44%

**∴ The correct answer is 44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective discount % = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer professes to sell goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
